evidence.note: Diagnosed that tied embedding/lm_head duplicated weights waste checkpoint space and patched save/load to reconstruct it, buying capacity within the byte cap; then empirically tested 17 vs 18 layers, found 18 exceeds 32MB (~31MB at 17), and chose 17 to maximize capacity under the cap — a deliberate size↔capacity tradeoff.
When full training failed because torch.compile/Triton needed a C compiler, correctly diagnosed the cause and switched to COMPILE=0 (eager + flash attention) rather than retrying blindly.

Long passive monitoring of a single 10k-iteration run that steadily improved; no divergence/overshoot arose so little reactive correction was needed — adaptation here was mostly waiting, not lever-changing.

On reaching local bpb 0.982936 (a razor-thin margin vs held-out variance), diagnosed that quantization loss + held-out gap made this unsafe and launched continuation fine-tuning from the DEQUANTIZED checkpoint with fresh AdamW/low LR, improvement-gated saves — a targeted correction to buy headroom.

Continuation compounded margin from 0.9829 → 0.9775, updating the checkpoint only on validation improvement; treated headroom below threshold as the objective rather than stopping at the first passing number.

reasoning: The agent showed genuine constraint-diagnosis adaptation: sizing depth to the byte cap, deduplicating tied weights to reclaim capacity, fixing the compile failure at its root, and — most tellingly — recognizing a thin bpb margin as a quantization/held-out risk and running dequantized continuation fine-tuning to build compounding headroom (steps 54-69). This exceeds a single-lever reaction (level 5) and reflects reasoning about the size↔capacity↔quant-loss frontier (level 8). It falls short of 10 because it never faced or had to abandon a diverging/dead-end run — the first big run largely worked, so most of the trajectory was passive monitoring rather than multi-run frontier optimization.
